question.problem:
The linear transformation $T$ and the vector $b\in {R}^{4}$ are given below. Determine if there exists a vector $x\in {R}^{4}$ such that $T(x)=b.$
In the affirmative case, find the value of $w+x-z,$ where $w,x,y,z$ are the components of $x.$  

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}w \\ x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}w+3z-x-2y \\ 4x-2w+y-6z \\ 3w+5x+10z-16y \\ 5y-w-3z-x\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & 5 & -16 & 10 \\ -1 & -1 & 5 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Since $T$ is the standard matix of $T,$ we have $\text{Im}(T)=\text{Col}(T).$ In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Im}(T),$ we need to check if the equation $Tx=b$ is consistent. 

So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[T\,|\,b]$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 5 & -16 & 10 & 4 \\ -1 & -1 & 5 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -10 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-4{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 & -20 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 12\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the fourth equation, we get the false statement $0=12.$ Therefore, the system is inconsistent, and we conclude that  $b\notin \text{Im}(T).$
